record.final_answer:
Four SKUs need reordering. They're at or below their reorder level once stock from both warehouses is added up:

| SKU | Stock | Reorder level |
|---|---|---|
| BX-100 | 23 (north 14 + south 9) | 25 |
| CL-310 | 5 (north 3 + south 2) | 5 |
| EN-512 | 0 | 10 |
| GH-118 | 7 | 12 |

BX-220 (40), DR-045 (120) and FT-760 (33) are above their levels. I added the stock up by hand as well and got the same list.

The plain `python3 restock.py exports/stock-2026-10-27.csv` command from the README fails. The export starts with a hidden byte-order mark, so the script reads the first column as `\ufeffsku` and stops with "column 'sku' not found". I didn't touch the file or the script. The script already takes an encoding option, and this command worked:

```
python3 restock.py exports/stock-2026-10-27.csv --encoding utf-8-sig
```

I saved this to memory so later sessions can get past the error. Future exports from the portal will probably have the same mark. If you want the README command to work as written, the script could default to `utf-8-sig`.
